title: First working transistor (point-contact)
place: Murray Hill, New Jersey, United States
summary: Bell Labs built a tiny device to switch and amplify electric signals.
why: A fundamental building block of modern electronics.
interchange: Herbert Mataré and Heinrich Welker independently built a point-contact transistor in Paris in 1948

notes.problem: 'Basis of all modern electronics' overclaims; source: 'one of the fundamental building blocks of modern electronics'.
Source documents an independent 1948 invention by Mataré and Welker; interchange was empty.
'Transistor invented' ignores Lilienfeld's 1925-28 field-effect transistor patents named in the source; source supports 'The first working device was a point-contact transistor invented in 1947'.
